Lead: VP of Search & Data (Maya Alvarez). Problem statement: replace brittle keyword search across 500k+ clinical notes, improve recall for rare disease mentions and reduce false positives from templated notes. Current infra: Elasticsearch cluster + in-house BM25 reranker; considering vector-based pipelines for embeddings + learned reranker. Key constraints: HIPAA, strict audit trails, per-query provenance, and ability to run in customer VPC or on-prem air-gapped option. User quotes: "We need <100ms median rerank at top-10 for triage flows; cost per query ideally <$0.015 average across mixed traffic." AE notes: prefer small CPU-friendly reranker for re-ranking stage (<=200M params) and 1536-d embedding vectors for storage efficiency. Interested in Redwood's KV caching and prefix hit rates for repeated query patterns. They asked about automatic fallback to smaller models under load and integration with Okta + SCIM.

Recent ask: network diagram + BAA for legal; will run a 6-week POC indexing 500k documents (de-identified set first, then PHI under BAA). They want traceability: token-level request/response logs to SIEM (Splunk) and immutable audit trail. Also asked about quantized model support and on-prem GPU options for private deployment.

Customer tone: pragmatic, cost-aware, security-first. Multiple internal stakeholders: Product (Maya), Security (Ethan Liu), Infra (Kavita Rao), Clinical SME (Dr. Ben Cho).

requirements_summary: High-scale clinical document search: 500k-2M docs (mix of notes, PDFs, scans -> OCR text). Need embeddings index with hybrid retrieval (BM25 + dense) and learned reranker. Latency targets: median end-to-end (retrieve + rerank) <120ms for triage UI, p95 <400ms. Throughput: 200 QPS peak with burst to 1k QPS. Cost sensitivity: target cost per query <$0.02 for avg workload. Must support HIPAA, VPC/on-prem, KMS-managed keys, per-request audit logs forwarded to Splunk, and ability to pin model versions for evaluation and rollback. POC acceptance criteria: F1 improvement on retrieval + reranking benchmark vs current baseline and meeting latency SLOs under 20% load increase.
